EMERGENCY RULES. 21 1. An agency may adopt emergency rules under section 17A.4, 22 subsection 3, and section 17A.5, subsection 2, paragraph 23 “b”, providing for additions, exceptions, or amendments to 24 uniform rules on agency procedure adopted by the administrative 25 rules coordinator pursuant to section 17A.24. The rules 26 shall be effective immediately upon filing unless a later 27 date is specified in the rules, but no later than June 30, 28 2026. However, rules adopted by the department of revenue or 29 the property assessment appeal board relating to contested 30 cases shall be effective no later than December 31, 2026. Any 31 rules adopted in accordance with this subsection shall also be 32 published as a notice of intended action as provided in section 33 17A.4. 34 2. Section 17A.7, subsections 2 and 3, Code 2026, are 1 amended to read as follows: 2 2. a. Beginning January 1, 2027, each agency shall conduct 3 an ongoing and comprehensive review of all of the agency’s 4 rules. The goal of the review is the identification and 5 elimination of all rules of the agency that are outdated, 6 redundant, or inconsistent or incompatible with statute or its 7 own rules or those of other agencies. Over each five-year 8 period of time, an agency shall perform a retrospective 9 analysis that includes a comprehensive evaluation and rigorous 10 cost-benefit analysis of each existing chapter of rules to 11 determine whether the benefits the rules are intended to 12 achieve are being realized, whether those benefits justify 13 the costs imposed by the rules, and whether there are less 14 restrictive alternatives to accomplish those benefits. 15 b. The administrative rules coordinator may adopt a schedule 16 for agencies to conduct reviews under this subsection that 17 staggers the reviews evenly over each five-year period. If the 18 administrative rules coordinator does so, the administrative 19 rules coordinator shall publish the schedule on the internet 20 site established or designated under paragraph “c” . 21 c. When the agency completes the five-year review of the 22 agency’s rules, the agency shall provide a written summary of 23 the results to the administrative rules coordinator and the 24 administrative rules review committee. The administrative 25 rules coordinator shall publish each summary on an internet 26 site established or designated for purposes of this subsection. 27 The summary shall include all of the following for each chapter 28 of rules: 29 a. (1) The intended benefits of the rules and if the 30 benefits are being achieved. 31 b. (2) The costs imposed by the rules and if the costs 32 are justified by the benefits identified in paragraph “a” 33 subparagraph (1) . 34 c. (3) Less restrictive alternatives to the rules and an 35 -7- SF 2463.3888 (1) 91 je/ko 7/ 11 analysis of how other states regulate the activities addressed 1 by the chapter. 2 3. a. Each chapter of rules is rescinded five years after 3 the date on which the most recent regulatory readoption of 4 the chapter as a whole became effective. A chapter rescinded 5 in this manner ceases to be effective as of the date of 6 rescission. The date of rescission of a chapter under this 7 subsection shall not be altered if such date falls on a 8 Saturday, Sunday, or holiday. 9 b. Before or after such rescission under paragraph “a” 10 occurs, the agency that adopted the chapter may adopt complete 11 a regulatory readoption of the chapter anew after completing 12 a retrospective analysis as described in subsection 2 . Such 13 adoption A regulatory readoption shall be subject to the 14 rulemaking process under this chapter , including but not 15 limited to sections 17A.4, 17A.4A, and 17A.5 . An agency 16 adopting completing a regulatory readoption of a chapter 17 anew as described in this subsection shall do so from a zero 18 base. Adoption A regulatory readoption of a chapter anew as 19 described in this subsection shall not include notation in 20 a rulemaking document published in the Iowa administrative 21 bulletin all amendments to the chapter found necessary or 22 appropriate by the agency during the agency’s comprehensive 23 review and retroactive analysis of the chapter pursuant to 24 subsection 2 that have not yet been adopted by the agency. A 25 regulatory readoption of a chapter shall include notations 26 of additions to or deletions from the language of the prior 27 chapter in the item statements in any rulemaking document 28 published in the Iowa administrative bulletin . The agency 29 shall indicate in the preamble of the rulemaking document 30 that the document is part of the regulatory readoption of the 31 chapter.
